result_text:
I fixed the three broken default scoping conventions in `ScopingConventions.java`, so the affected files now land in their intended scopes. The full `codeanalyzer` suite passes (334 run, 0 failures, 3 skipped), including a new test I added.

The changes, all in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`:

- **Generated HTML pages:** the pkgdown, Doxygen and `<meta name="generator">` rules now use `(html|htm|xhtml)` instead of `(html|html|xhtml)`. That also fixes the duplicated `html` in the alternation.
- **.NET documentation XML and JavaScript generated files:** the path patterns are now `.*[.]xml` and `.*[.]js` instead of `.*/[.]xml` and `.*/[.]js`, which required a slash before the dot. The content rules are unchanged, so an ordinary `.js` or `.xml` file still needs the `<doc>` or `// Generated by` line to match.
- **Gradle JavaScript scripts:** the pattern is now `.*[-]gradle[.]js` instead of `.*[.][-]gradle[.]js`, so `build-gradle.js` matches and `build.gradle` still matches its own rule.

I added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`. It covers a `.htm` pkgdown, Doxygen and generator page, `.html` and `.xhtml` still matching, `MyAssembly.xml` with `<doc>`, `app.js` with `// Generated by`, `build-gradle.js`, `.-gradle.js` and `build.gradle`. It also checks that hand-written `.htm`, `.js` and `.xml` files stay unmatched. Nothing is committed.
